plan.topic: Unproven plague 'cures' circulating online (AFP Fact Check, Oct 9) vs what actually treats plague
plan.angle: Hook: 'Prepper kits and unproven pills: AFP Fact Check reports dubious plague cures spreading online (Oct 8, 2026).' Answer within 10 s: WHO says antibiotics and supportive care work against plague when it's diagnosed in time, and doctors prescribe them. Experts told AFP not to take antibiotics without a known exposure. Health authorities give preventive antibiotics to close contacts. No product names, no remedy list, no drug names or doses. Add the dated Irkutsk status hedge. Close with the urgent-contact line and 'If you're worried, talk to a health professional.' Title: 'Plague Cures Online: What Actually Treats Plague, According to CDC and WHO #shorts'.

plan.why: The bold myth-busting piece of the day. AFP published only on Oct 9, so we're early, and it builds on the 'Is plague curable?' Reel that reached 102 accounts. | fact-check: The AFP piece is real ('Unproven cures pushed online amid plague concerns', syndicated by CP24/CTV on Oct 8, 2026), but it doesn't mention garlic, herbs or home remedies. It covers influencers and preppers selling a roughly $300 kit and an X post listing supplements and drugs. Experts told AFP ivermectin would be ineffective and warned against taking antibiotics without a known exposure. The hook has to match that, and the date has to be the AFP publication date (Oct 8 per syndication, not Oct 9, unless AFP's own page says otherwise). Don't name the influencer or list the remedies. Use WHO's own wording on treatment: 'Antibiotics and supportive therapy are effective against plague if patients are diagnosed in time', and pneumonic plague 'can be fatal within 18 to 24 hours… if left untreated'. The experts' warning against taking antibiotics without exposure directly supports the no-stockpiling guardrail, so include it.

package.description:
AFP Fact Check (Oct 8, 2026) reported an unproven ~$300 prepper kit promoted in posts tagged plague, reportedly with ivermectin inside. A plague researcher told AFP ivermectin is never really used for a bacterial disease.
WHO says antibiotics and supportive therapy are effective if patients are diagnosed in time; CDC says plague can be cured with antibiotics, but treatment must be given quickly.
Status: Oct 8, 2026, Rospotrebnadzor said no plague case registered in Irkutsk oblast; WHO said it doesn't know the cause of death. Oct 9, the Irkutsk oblast governor said contact monitoring found no dangerous pathogens. Not confirmed isn't ruled out.
Possible exposure plus fever, cough, shortness of breath or chest pain? Contact a doctor or local health authority urgently.

factcheck.summary: I checked every factual claim against its cited source, and all of them hold up. AFP via CP24 (Oct 8, 2026) supports the US$300 kit, the #plague hashtag, the ivermectin claim, plague researcher Paul Keim's line that "ivermectin is never really used for a bacterial disease" and infectious disease specialist Isaac Bogoch's warning not to take antibiotics "without known exposure". The WHO fact sheet (page dated Sep 29, 2026) carries the s3 quote word for word, the 18–24 hour line for untreated pneumonic plague, and chemoprophylaxis for close contacts of pneumonic plague patients. The CDC About page (last reviewed Aug 24, 2026) says "Plague can be cured with antibiotics, but these must be given promptly." The CDC symptoms page lists fever, cough, shortness of breath and chest pain. The AP/PBS article (Oct 8) supports Rospotrebnadzor saying "no case of plague has been registered" and "pneumonia of unknown origin", and WHO saying it doesn't know the cause and asking for more information. CGTN (Oct 9) supports the governor saying contact monitoring was complete and that nearly 5,000 lab tests found no dangerous pathogens. A fresh search found no official status change after Oct 9. The safety lines are in place: the urgency line, the worried line and the no-self-treatment message. I've listed 4 minor fixes on scope and wording, plus a length note: the script is about 235 words, over the 170-word guide but well under the 178 s hard limit.

issues.claim: the Irkutsk oblast governor said monitoring of all contacts was complete, with no dangerous pathogens found
issues.problem: Scope is slightly widened. Per CGTN, the governor said 'Medical monitoring of all contacts has also been completed, while nearly 5,000 laboratory tests found no dangerous pathogenic microorganisms.' The 'no pathogens' finding applies to the lab tests, not to the monitoring itself.
issues.fix: On Oct 9, the Irkutsk oblast governor said monitoring of all contacts was complete, and nearly 5,000 lab tests found no dangerous pathogens.

issues.problem: Rospotrebnadzor's actual wording is 'no case of plague has been registered'. The on-screen text credits it with a paraphrase that doesn't match the narration, and it leaves out WHO's same-day position.
issues.fix: NO PLAGUE CASE REGISTERED: ROSPOTREBNADZOR, OCT 8, 2026 · WHO: CAUSE NOT KNOWN (keep 'NOT KNOWN' and 'NO PLAGUE CASE' on the same caption screen)

issues.claim: ...called the death pneumonia of unknown origin. WHO said that day it doesn't know what caused her death
issues.problem: 'Her' has no antecedent in the Short, because the person who died is never introduced. The listener may not know who 'her' refers to.
issues.fix: Status: on Oct 8, 2026, Russia's health watchdog Rospotrebnadzor said no case of plague has been registered in Irkutsk oblast and called a lab worker's death pneumonia of unknown origin. WHO said that day it doesn't know what caused her death and asked Russia for more information.

issues.claim: Prepper kits and unproven pills ... reportedly with ivermectin inside
issues.problem: AFP reports that the kit also contains doxycycline, an antibiotic that is actually used for plague. Calling all the kit's contents 'unproven pills' without mentioning this overgeneralizes. The real problem AFP describes is self-treatment without a known exposure.
issues.fix: s2: AFP Fact Check reported on Oct 8, 2026: a kit for about $300, promoted in posts tagged plague, reportedly with the antibiotic doxycycline and ivermectin inside. A plague researcher told AFP ivermectin is never really used for a bacterial disease.

issues.problem: The narration is about 235 words (roughly 85–95 s), over the 170-word guide but under the 178 s hard limit. The title uses 2 abbreviations (CDC, WHO) where the guide allows 1. Both are craft points, not accuracy problems.
issues.fix: Optionally trim s6 by dropping 'Russia's health watchdog'. Title, if you want 1 abbreviation: Plague 'Cures' Online: What Actually Treats Plague, According to the CDC #shorts (only if s3 keeps CDC's wording as the lead)

Cleaned up ~15 simultaneous duplicate-layer cues (e.g. swoosh+whoosh or swell+whip firing at the same timestamp) by zeroing the redundant layer, trimmed the 4-effect cluster at 82.8s down to 3, pulled down a handful of cues that read 2–5 dB hotter than their neighbors during speech (i17, i18, i40, i76), and quieted the music/SFX swell under the "Not confirmed ≠ ruled out" line to match the serious-moment rule. Added three bespoke accents: a single heartbeat for the 18–24h urgency stat, a calm chime for the WHO Oct 8 citation, and a low string stab for the "not confirmed ≠ ruled out" correction.
